Keep every row in order. Preserve all [[I]], [[B]], [[SC]] emphasis markers, [[Nnumber]] note markers and explicit source line counts. Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 41, "heading": "CHAPTER 39. WICKFIELD AND HEEP", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u041-b0126", "target": "Его рассказ о себе имел по крайней мере одно приятное последствие: он убрал свою руку, чтобы ещё раз обнять себя под подбородком. Освободившись от него, я решил держаться в стороне; и мы пошли обратно рядом, почти ничего больше не говоря по дороге. Было ли его настроение приподнято моим сообщением или тем, что он предался этим воспоминаниям, я не знаю; но какое-то влияние его подняло. За обедом он говорил больше обычного; спросил свою мать (снятую с дежурства с той минуты, как мы вошли в дом), не становится ли он слишком стар для холостяка; и однажды посмотрел на Агнес так, что я отдал бы всё, что у меня было, за разрешение сбить его с ног.", "source_sha256": "0894ba529ea74cae42f0b66828c9282cd7c1c7a0e73cb25d04fdc116ee96e7a7", "target_id": "ru-en85-u041-b0126", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "16480f33894541116202648ef5710fc9887ff4b78d4cd39c226b042a479fb091"}, {"source_id": "en85-u041-b0127", "target": "Когда после обеда мы остались втроём, мужчины, он стал ещё более смелым. Он почти не пил вина; и я полагаю, на него действовала просто наглость торжества, быть может, разгорячённая искушением выставить её напоказ, которое создавало моё присутствие.", "source_sha256": "34aca888086706bf5f278d70581cea8b7ed69e1d0807f91ff5720f9da217e5be", "target_id": "ru-en85-u041-b0127", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "1776dfa9083d9384eabdfaab99ea5eebf39ca1a2a0e88a3ebbad91e1d9f59562"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 39, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u041-b0128", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I had observed yesterday, that he tried to entice Mr. Wickfield to drink; and, interpreting the look which Agnes had given me as she went out, had limited myself to one glass, and then proposed that we should follow her. I would have done so again today; but Uriah was too quick for me.", "sha256": "6c6ae8e102e7bbd751ade8a69e85e238838e599115bbdd85dc87617c10bb5823", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[128]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0129", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘We seldom see our present visitor, sir,’ he said, addressing Mr. Wickfield, sitting, such a contrast to him, at the end of the table, ‘and I should propose to give him welcome in another glass or two of wine, if you have no objections. Mr. Copperfield, your elth and appiness!’", "sha256": "d74bb721dfc307460a796a7fc2a97c1ad69c96ad02209eaddb00221a5f35217f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[129]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0130", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I was obliged to make a show of taking the hand he stretched across to me; and then, with very different emotions, I took the hand of the broken gentleman, his partner.", "sha256": "4deddd5cfda3e44060ab20caee13641a82fb2714b7005e1b148a1f1de662aa49", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[130]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0131", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Come, fellow-partner,’ said Uriah, ‘if I may take the liberty,—now, suppose you give us something or another appropriate to Copperfield!’", "sha256": "ebc7b49614000245d84a25df4e5b23ae7123c3d96a067b73bd352ca480320b58", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[131]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0132", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I pass over Mr. Wickfield’s proposing my aunt, his proposing Mr. Dick, his proposing Doctors’ Commons, his proposing Uriah, his drinking everything twice; his consciousness of his own weakness, the ineffectual effort that he made against it; the struggle between his shame in Uriah’s deportment, and his desire to conciliate him; the manifest exultation with which Uriah twisted and turned, and held him up before me. It made me sick at heart to see, and my hand recoils from writing it.", "sha256": "e80591e36733a585ec9095dc28b659e538a83be04887f1c25b71e239ba498bdf", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[132]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0133", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Come, fellow-partner!’ said Uriah, at last, ‘I’ll give you another one, and I umbly ask for bumpers, seeing I intend to make it the divinest of her sex.’", "sha256": "464975569c02da18fb16f2e03aa60f245ea10892a166b52e90827802c2193f0a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[133]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0134", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Her father had his empty glass in his hand. I saw him set it down, look at the picture she was so like, put his hand to his forehead, and shrink back in his elbow-chair.", "sha256": "b1cdac6faadcac21bbc5f0f0edb2cb2af1b245a29cb58cfba3de602faaa50e84", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[134]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0135", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I’m an umble individual to give you her elth,’ proceeded Uriah, ‘but I admire—adore her.’", "sha256": "4ff78708b17b2ce347f7d7420811da02d286d6501263f1a122245d2b2faf3617", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[135]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0136", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "No physical pain that her father’s grey head could have borne, I think, could have been more terrible to me, than the mental endurance I saw compressed now within both his hands.", "sha256": "18e50a27f0f83acc182db15093c612d9fbaed5ea5aeecf44e8103975cffe5cb9", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[136]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0137", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Agnes,’ said Uriah, either not regarding him, or not knowing what the nature of his action was, ‘Agnes Wickfield is, I am safe to say, the divinest of her sex. May I speak out, among friends? To be her father is a proud distinction, but to be her usband—’", "sha256": "ec58a8e6e5834ab816552a36bd7ad74636841c8c9eb860dbcbe7bbdb1dbfe194", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[137]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0138", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Spare me from ever again hearing such a cry, as that with which her father rose up from the table! ‘What’s the matter?’ said Uriah, turning of a deadly colour. ‘You are not gone mad, after all, Mr. Wickfield, I hope? If I say I’ve an ambition to make your Agnes my Agnes, I have as good a right to it as another man. I have a better right to it than any other man!’", "sha256": "2a98bde1b7588f1db974bcbdaf0b166002d8593162a3d1f8124e3469883ccdd4", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[138]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0139", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I had my arms round Mr. Wickfield, imploring him by everything that I could think of, oftenest of all by his love for Agnes, to calm himself a little. He was mad for the moment; tearing out his hair, beating his head, trying to force me from him, and to force himself from me, not answering a word, not looking at or seeing anyone; blindly striving for he knew not what, his face all staring and distorted—a frightful spectacle.", "sha256": "781bb854dc9541405ebe75d0db3461506bd7bbc36c49952862c4a9685028532f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[139]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0140", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I conjured him, incoherently, but in the most impassioned manner, not to abandon himself to this wildness, but to hear me. I besought him to think of Agnes, to connect me with Agnes, to recollect how Agnes and I had grown up together, how I honoured her and loved her, how she was his pride and joy. I tried to bring her idea before him in any form; I even reproached him with not having firmness to spare her the knowledge of such a scene as this. I may have effected something, or his wildness may have spent itself; but by degrees he struggled less, and began to look at me—strangely at first, then with recognition in his eyes. At length he said, ‘I know, Trotwood! My darling child and you—I know! But look at him!’", "sha256": "c1b918d330d8d7ea5dd9a5925313808fefb54c2f9483b4e004ee55fa23d3470c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[140]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0141", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "He pointed to Uriah, pale and glowering in a corner, evidently very much out in his calculations, and taken by surprise.", "sha256": "40b3dfa1b59acb4dbac4c66272f047f4f566ec3639ad4805c79f042bf09be200", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[141]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0142", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Look at my torturer,’ he replied. ‘Before him I have step by step abandoned name and reputation, peace and quiet, house and home.’", "sha256": "413c23864066e2bc6e5737d332b261d6632438ec6c8090f8befd3b2e3bfd2d6f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[142]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0143", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I have kept your name and reputation for you, and your peace and quiet, and your house and home too,’ said Uriah, with a sulky, hurried, defeated air of compromise. ‘Don’t be foolish, Mr. Wickfield. If I have gone a little beyond what you were prepared for, I can go back, I suppose? There’s no harm done.’", "sha256": "c080776c648d5d71a9dadaca73c22126c23f1a28c12a5b8aec4284394b3b8313", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[143]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0144", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I looked for single motives in everyone,’ said Mr. Wickfield, ‘and I was satisfied I had bound him to me by motives of interest. But see what he is—oh, see what he is!’", "sha256": "b33f386ccc106185a1cfd25ff1852808ea877766fa0e278a5e2fb8f756ca5455", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[144]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0145", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You had better stop him, Copperfield, if you can,’ cried Uriah, with his long forefinger pointing towards me. ‘He’ll say something presently—mind you!—he’ll be sorry to have said afterwards, and you’ll be sorry to have heard!’", "sha256": "d18e918c4f7bb78bcb62c5111150872df05b8a9e7e6de83382657e10676be4dc", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[145]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0146", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I’ll say anything!’ cried Mr. Wickfield, with a desperate air. ‘Why should I not be in all the world’s power if I am in yours?’", "sha256": "31e9081bc5d61235b32ac356c030bf91a14ff53a390cfe119674a10bbaafdcc0", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[146]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0147", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Mind! I tell you!’ said Uriah, continuing to warn me. ‘If you don’t stop his mouth, you’re not his friend! Why shouldn’t you be in all the world’s power, Mr. Wickfield? Because you have got a daughter. You and me know what we know, don’t we? Let sleeping dogs lie—who wants to rouse ‘em? I don’t. Can’t you see I am as umble as I can be? I tell you, if I’ve gone too far, I’m sorry. What would you have, sir?’", "sha256": "68505f569c2bdd298e72f7bdca0ea14bb5cdef65bb04003714e43d5863971982", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[147]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0148", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Oh, Trotwood, Trotwood!’ exclaimed Mr. Wickfield, wringing his hands. ‘What I have come down to be, since I first saw you in this house! I was on my downward way then, but the dreary, dreary road I have traversed since! Weak indulgence has ruined me. Indulgence in remembrance, and indulgence in forgetfulness. My natural grief for my child’s mother turned to disease; my natural love for my child turned to disease. I have infected everything I touched. I have brought misery on what I dearly love, I know—you know! I thought it possible that I could truly love one creature in the world, and not love the rest; I thought it possible that I could truly mourn for one creature gone out of the world, and not have some part in the grief of all who mourned. Thus the lessons of my life have been perverted! I have preyed on my own morbid coward heart, and it has preyed on me. Sordid in my grief, sordid in my love, sordid in my miserable escape from the darker side of both, oh see the ruin I am, and hate me, shun me!’", "sha256": "b6aa4d3c4621ca4c76dcf1bac0e95c82f7ec33d9aff29a5cd60d166393256962", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[148]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0149", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "He dropped into a chair, and weakly sobbed. The excitement into which he had been roused was leaving him. Uriah came out of his corner.", "sha256": "1a8215ff6aaf934eb4e7567ec3e461f41603bd536552f3335e3a376da31eff8f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[149]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0150", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I don’t know all I have done, in my fatuity,’ said Mr. Wickfield, putting out his hands, as if to deprecate my condemnation. ‘He knows best,’ meaning Uriah Heep, ‘for he has always been at my elbow, whispering me. You see the millstone that he is about my neck. You find him in my house, you find him in my business. You heard him, but a little time ago. What need have I to say more!’", "sha256": "4108b4bd2331853219bb8ff0f671f2ef56c8f3f2256198f4599ad2f58882fcd7", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[150]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0151", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You haven’t need to say so much, nor half so much, nor anything at all,’ observed Uriah, half defiant, and half fawning. ‘You wouldn’t have took it up so, if it hadn’t been for the wine. You’ll think better of it tomorrow, sir. If I have said too much, or more than I meant, what of it? I haven’t stood by it!’", "sha256": "a0dbecdd06bc4433f48af08d45e8079203e92dd3e0501e629e25faab85a6e3f8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[151]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0152", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The door opened, and Agnes, gliding in, without a vestige of colour in her face, put her arm round his neck, and steadily said, ‘Papa, you are not well. Come with me!’", "sha256": "6c60ef594143007c2931d85ac243c322f1ef3f8e673c0fe618dadb2318927059", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[152]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0153", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "He laid his head upon her shoulder, as if he were oppressed with heavy shame, and went out with her. Her eyes met mine for but an instant, yet I saw how much she knew of what had passed.", "sha256": "fc7a6a5a9144d8e196027388da5c9535669c2170d9f8b34be4c88220ed317a3a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[153]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0154", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I didn’t expect he’d cut up so rough, Master Copperfield,’ said Uriah. ‘But it’s nothing. I’ll be friends with him tomorrow. It’s for his good. I’m umbly anxious for his good.’", "sha256": "ffccb9c87ae2f3d591f4adec1083cdbc67c48c964c673cbe5ac487eb675ec52c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[154]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0155", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I gave him no answer, and went upstairs into the quiet room where Agnes had so often sat beside me at my books. Nobody came near me until late at night. I took up a book, and tried to read. I heard the clocks strike twelve, and was still reading, without knowing what I read, when Agnes touched me.", "sha256": "b03780babe1d6aadf1d80052787553bbba80920ccd76f9f7cb6a8d5b95514bb3", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[155]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0156", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You will be going early in the morning, Trotwood! Let us say good-bye, now!’", "sha256": "ed5cedee5f536f747d8e1a6f89302e8f0b1c289df863bcb47db52aca6d6e98cf", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[156]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0157", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "She had been weeping, but her face then was so calm and beautiful!", "sha256": "c067cee962b613ec0297d5567d34f130aec8c6d38893fad2f5851201932ab65f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[157]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0158", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Heaven bless you!’ she said, giving me her hand.", "sha256": "9e0b397e44583baf53a33a3d5eefc50068c3e2cf334aa812f9213668dd73ea62", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[158]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u041-b0159", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Dearest Agnes!’ I returned, ‘I see you ask me not to speak of tonight—but is there nothing to be done?’", "sha256": "dc054ee1645645592475a2ac60082287c02b3f3e83ec35ad6c0eeb705f7df0c9", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[46]/p[159]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
